design.decision: When behind, bid more aggressively, because the doubled score makes a big made contract the fastest way back (and a set doubles the loss too).
design.opponent: Revealed the first time it applies; the leading team knows a trailing opponent swings harder and can defend to set them.
design.rationale: The game is lopsided (the median final margin is about half the winner's score) and the brief asks for comeback pieces; this is the most direct one, and because it also doubles sets it rewards a decision rather than handing out points.
design.draftText: ×2 contract multiplier if your team has fewer points than the opponents
design.hooks: New trigger event `behind`: true when your team's run score is below the opponents' at the start of the round, fixed before bidding and never re-checked during the round; any payoff can use this general run-state condition.

critic.concerns: Generated text reads as a result checked at scoring, but the hook snapshots the run score at the start of the round; the text template must state that timing, e.g. 'if your team is behind when the round begins'. It is dead for a leading team and changes bidding only indirectly.

text: ×2 contract multiplier if your team is behind when the round begins
